newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products mixed despite crude gains.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products mixed despite crude gains.

text.p: Singapore oil products closed mixed despite strong gains to crude and gas oil on the London markets, traders said on Wednesday.

Gas oil edged up only slightly on sharply higher values on the IPE which traded to a five-year high at $222.75 per tonne. Players reported that September cargoes are tight but market is better supplied for October.

Jet fuel firmed on higher gas oil and swaps values. October swaps were traded at $30.00. The first month swaps jet fuel/gas oil spread has firmed slightly to $2.30 from an early week low of under $2.00.

But market remained depressed on talks of high stocks in Singapore. One trader estimated that there are about 1 million barrels of jet stored in Singapore by about three or four companies. Sri Lanka has issued a gas oil and jet fuel buy tender for arrival in October 11-12.
The light distillates were mixed with naphtha levels supported by the overnight rise in crude but gasoline continued to be talked lower.
A Dutch trader's offer for 50,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded gasoline lifting October 1-5 at $21.65 was bought by a Japanese trading house.
Buyers for the same timing were also seen and bids were raised from $21.20 to $21.65 with another 50,000 barrel traded at the same level.
Singapore high sulphur fuel oil prices eased despite crude gains. Near market close, 60,000 tonnes of 180 cst cargoes were traded between $112.50 and $113.50 for loading in the first half of October.
Two cargoes were purchased by a Japanese trader and the third cargo by a European major. Traders said agressive offers emerged late Wednesday caused prices to ease.
